title: Quiz: DMAIC Framework and Root Cause Analysis Tools

questions.text: A Six Sigma team discovers that 78% of customer returns are caused by just 2 of 12 product defect types. Which tool revealed this finding?
questions.explanation: The Pareto chart ranks defects by frequency and shows the cumulative percentage. Finding that 78% of returns come from 2 defect types is a classic Pareto (80/20) finding.

questions.text: The Control phase of DMAIC is primarily concerned with:
options: Identifying the root cause of variation
Sustaining the gains made in the Improve phase
Defining the scope of the problem
questions.explanation: The Control phase sustains improvements by implementing control charts, control plans, and dashboards to ensure the process does not regress after the project closes.

questions.text: A Fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram alone is sufficient to identify the true root cause of a quality problem.
questions.explanation: The Fishbone diagram generates hypotheses about possible causes — it is a brainstorming tool. Confirmation requires data collection and statistical analysis (hypothesis tests, regression, etc.) in the Analyze phase.

questions.text: In the DMAIC Measure phase, a team discovers their measurement system has 38% GR&R. What should they do?
options: Proceed with capability analysis — 38% is close to 30%
Improve the measurement system before collecting baseline performance data
Skip the Measure phase and move to Analyze
Widen the specification limits to compensate
questions.explanation: A measurement system with > 30% GR&R is unacceptable. Data collected with it is unreliable. The team must fix the measurement system in the Measure phase before any further analysis is valid.

questions.text: A data engineering team's ETL pipeline has a high error rate. They draw a Fishbone and identify 'analysts use different transformation scripts' as a cause. Which 6M bone does this belong to?
questions.explanation: Different transformation scripts represent inconsistent Methods (procedures/processes). When the method is not standardised, variation and errors increase.
